chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: Bop glasses, bow ties and fashion
summary: Monk, Dizzy and the dress fashions; Harold Fox's shop.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: We said that Monk originated, in Jazz circles anyway, wearing the heavy rimmed glasses. He had some with bamboo frames or something. That he actually was ahead of Dizzy in that.

Well, he might have been. Because I really don't know. I can't say one way or the other, whether he did create this or not. I know I've seen Dizzy with those type of glasses. But then again, I don't know what it is with Dizzy, because he tells me he can see with... I always see him with them damn glasses on, it makes me think he can't see or he need help. I don't know.

Well, it's funny, because at the time when he started wearing those heavy-rimmed glasses, and they became known as Bop Glasses, just as we had Bop Bowties and this and that, a lot of people used to buy those heavy-framed glasses who really didn't need glasses, and just had window panes in them, just to be wearing those glasses. Because it became the fashion...
McGhee (12/6) - 41
I don't know why glasses became a Fashion all of a sudden. I don't know why. I don't know how that happened to come about.
Well, I think it's because Dizzy was such a flamboyant character, people copied what he did.
You think that was it?

Yeah, because the beret and the goatee, you know, and people began wearing them who were into this music or who were followers of this music. But it's true that musicians have always been trend-setters in dress and things like that...
Yes...
A different style of clothing. At that time, if you remember, we had the cardigan jackets, no lapels, and people started wearing those -- in that period.

Oh yeah. They had that during the time of, say... Like in the Forties, the Early Forties or the Mid-Forties... Yeah, because they would have the uniforms. I remember once I was out in California, and I went out and bought some uniforms for the band, and they all had jackets, cardigan jackets and trousers and so forth -- which was very nice and made the band look decent. But that didn't change none of the... It didn't change the music.
No, it was just the outer effects.
McGhee (12/6) - 42
Yeah, the outer effects.
Do you remember Harold Fox's tailor shop in Chicago?
Yeah, sure I remember it. Yeah, I got a couple of suits from him. I got a pretty brown suit that I got from him.
[PAUSE]
You know, Harold Fox used to sell mail order, too, through Downbeat, and he used to sell the Bop Bowties and different things like that.
Yeah.

And I remember other mail order outfits selling the Bop Glasses, with the window panes in Downbeat. They used to advertise them... I guess they even had goatees you could paste on if you couldn't grow your own goatee.
Well, I don't know about that. I never went in for that. I used to wear a goatee, but that was because... That's what I wanted to show you...
[PAUSE]
